Why: Step 4 is the first step that decides the mark, and it does not break. Premise A4 is doing the work, and the AI rightly calls it added: a normalized ledger in which each removal costs 0.1/N, the whole group’s cumulative cost stays at 0.1, and that never crosses one case’s continuing harm of 0.5. Those magnitudes do not follow from the lines step 4 cites. Those lines require only that lost coupling and lost diversity be positive and enter the measurement; they do not force a crossing before this finite sequence ends. Nor does any line rule the ledger out. The saturation sentences assert that a crossing must occur, but that assertion is the live KS-32.5 claim under test, not a derived cost function, and the measure that would make the crossing necessary is named as owed. Steps 1–3 and 5–6 also use unsettled choices, including Debts 25 and 26, but they do not decide the mark: without A4’s unresolved ledger the brake is not shown to fail, and later steps only apply that ledger. The AI’s own note that step 4 is weakest is right; read as a break, it is not. The road therefore does not fire the brake’s failure as a closed result.
